design.quote: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive optimized HF therapy (up to four drugs: sacubitril/valsartan, empagliflozin, ivabradine, ferric carboxymaltose) or placebo in a double-blind setting.

population.value: Patients with stage 4 solid tumours with a life expectancy of 1-6 months receiving specialized palliative care, meeting at least two cardiovascular risk criteria and at least one criterion for functional limitation
population.quote: Patients with stage 4 solid tumours with a life expectancy of 1-6 months receiving specialized palliative care were enrolled. Patients were required to meet at least two cardiovascular risk criteria and at least one criterion for functional limitation.

sample_size.quote: In five centres, 93 patients were randomized.

intervention.value: Optimized HF therapy (up to four drugs: sacubitril/valsartan, empagliflozin, ivabradine, ferric carboxymaltose)
intervention.quote: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive optimized HF therapy (up to four drugs: sacubitril/valsartan, empagliflozin, ivabradine, ferric carboxymaltose) or placebo in a double-blind setting.

comparator.quote: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive optimized HF therapy (up to four drugs: sacubitril/valsartan, empagliflozin, ivabradine, ferric carboxymaltose) or placebo in a double-blind setting.

follow_up.quote: The primary hierarchical endpoint included: (i) days alive and able to wash oneself, (ii) ability to walk 4 m, and (iii) self-reported patient global assessment (PGA) of subjective well-being, during the 30-day placebo-controlled phase.

primary_findings.quote: The primary endpoint did not differ between groups (win ratio 0.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.57-1.58; P = .83).
primary_findings.outcome: Primary hierarchical endpoint (days alive and able to wash oneself, ability to walk 4 m, self-reported PGA of subjective well-being)

primary_findings.quote: Overall, mortality was 32% at 30 days (not different between groups).
In patients alive at 30 days, HF therapy reduced N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels by 41% (P = .040).
primary_findings.outcome: NT-proBNP levels in survivors at 30 days

primary_findings.quote: In patients alive at 30 days, HF therapy increased left ventricular ejection fraction by 2.9% (P = .036).
primary_findings.outcome: Left ventricular ejection fraction in survivors at 30 days

primary_findings.quote: In patients alive at 30 days, HF therapy improved PGA scores (odds ratio 0.22, 95% CI 0.06-0.75; P = .016).
primary_findings.outcome: Patient global assessment (PGA) scores in survivors at 30 days

limitations_stated.value: High early mortality in the study population
limitations_stated.quote: In a population with advanced cancer receiving specialized palliative care and high early mortality, optimized HF therapy did not improve patients' self-care ability.

limitations_stated.value: Results among survivors at 30 days are hypothesis generating and need validation
limitations_stated.quote: Among survivors at 30 days, improvements in quality of life measures and cardiac biomarkers suggest potential benefit of individualized HF therapy, which is hypothesis generating and needs validation.
